questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: "The bank will waive the processing fee on all home loans sanctioned during the festival month," said the bank's chairman.

Assumptions:
I. The waiver will attract more home-loan borrowers to the bank during the festival month.
II. The bank charges no other fee on home loans.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: A fee waiver for a limited period is meant to draw more borrowers in that period, so I is implicit. Whether the bank charges other fees has nothing to do with the waiver, so II is not implicit.
steps: Purpose of a limited-period waiver ⇒ more borrowers: I
Other fees are irrelevant ⇒ II not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both accept an irrelevant claim; Neither ignores the purpose of the offer.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only assumption I is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: A university's notice: "Apply for the merit scholarship before 15 July. Applications received after 15 July will not be considered."

Assumptions:
I. The university expects to receive applications for the merit scholarship.
II. Every application received before 15 July will be accepted for the scholarship.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: A notice inviting applications is issued only if applications are expected (I). The notice says late applications will not be considered; it does not follow that every timely application will be accepted. Being considered is not the same as being granted the scholarship, so II is not implicit.
steps: Inviting applications ⇒ applications expected: I
'Not considered if late' does not mean 'accepted if on time' ⇒ II not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both confuse 'considered' with 'accepted'; Neither ignores why the notice was issued.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only assumption I is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: "To cut paper use, the office will print all internal documents on both sides of the sheet from Monday," said the office manager.

Assumptions:
I. The office's printers can print on both sides of a sheet, or can be made to do so.
II. Printing on both sides of a sheet uses fewer sheets than printing on one side.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: The plan can work only if the printers can print on both sides (I), and it cuts paper use only if double-sided printing needs fewer sheets (II). Both are taken for granted.
steps: Plan must be practicable ⇒ I
Plan must serve its purpose ⇒ II
solution.why_others_wrong: Each 'Only' option drops one of two things the plan rests on.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both I and II are implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: "The city's new metro line will open to the public on 1 March," announced the metro corporation.

Assumptions:
I. Once the line opens, all the buses on the same route will run empty.
II. The new line will carry more passengers than any other metro line in the city.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: The announcement only gives an opening date. It does not need buses to lose every passenger (I is extreme), or the new line to carry more passengers than every other line (II).
steps: Opening date only ⇒ no claim about buses: I not implicit
No comparison with other lines ⇒ II not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Each of the other options accepts a sweeping prediction that the announcement does not depend on.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Neither I nor II is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: The government has made it compulsory for every new two-wheeler sold in the country to be fitted with an anti-lock braking system.

Assumptions:
I. Two-wheelers without an anti-lock braking system will stop being used on the roads at once.
II. Anti-lock braking systems make two-wheelers safer to ride.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: A safety device is made compulsory only if it is believed to improve safety (II). The rule covers only new two-wheelers, so it does not assume that older two-wheelers without the system will vanish from the roads at once (I).
steps: Compulsory fitting ⇒ the device is believed to help: II
Rule is for new vehicles only ⇒ I not implicit
solution.why_others_wrong: Only I and Both read the rule as applying to existing vehicles; Neither ignores why the device is required.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only assumption II is implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two assumptions. An assumption is something supposed or taken for granted by the person making the statement. Decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement: A hospital has started an SMS service that tells each patient in the outpatient queue when his or her turn is about 15 minutes away.

Assumptions:
I. Patients waiting in the outpatient queue have phones that can receive SMS messages.
II. Some patients would rather spend part of their waiting time away from the queue area.

options.text: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit

solution.concept: Implicit assumption: what the speaker must take for granted
solution.explanation: An SMS alert is useful only if the patients can receive SMS messages (I). The point of telling a patient that the turn is 15 minutes away is to let him or her wait elsewhere and come back in time (II).
steps: Service works only if SMS can be received ⇒ I
Purpose: patients need not wait in the queue area ⇒ II
solution.why_others_wrong: Each 'Only' option drops one of two things the service depends on.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both I and II are implicit

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: Every member of the city chess club has a national rating. No member of the city chess club is under 10 years of age. Arnav is 9 years old.

Conclusions:
I. Arnav is not a member of the city chess club.
II. Arnav does not have a national rating.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: No member is under 10, and Arnav is 9, so he is not a member (I). The statement says that every member has a rating, not that only members have ratings, so Arnav may or may not have one (II does not follow).
steps: No member under 10; Arnav is 9 ⇒ not a member: I
'Every member has a rating' does not mean 'only members do' ⇒ II does not follow
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both reverse 'every member has a rating'; Neither misses the direct age rule.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only conclusion I follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: A cinema hall has 240 seats. For the 6 pm show, exactly 180 tickets were sold, one ticket for each seat, and no seat was sold twice.

Conclusions:
I. At least 60 seats were unsold for the 6 pm show.
II. 75% of the seats were sold for the 6 pm show.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: Unsold seats = 240 − 180 = 60, so 'at least 60' is true (I). 180 ÷ 240 = 0.75 = 75% (II).
steps: Sold share = 180 ÷ 240 = 75% ⇒ II
solution.why_others_wrong: Each 'Only' option drops one of two direct calculations; Neither ignores both.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: The price of a kilogram of rice at a shop rose from ₹50 to ₹60 this month.

Conclusions:
I. The price of rice at the shop rose by 20% this month.
II. Rice was in short supply this month.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: The rise is ₹10 on ₹50, that is 20% (I). The statement gives no reason for the rise; a shortage is one possible reason among many, so II does not follow.
steps: Cause of the rise not stated ⇒ II does not follow
solution.why_others_wrong: Only II and Both assume a cause; Neither ignores the direct calculation.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only conclusion I follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: Some of the trains that leave the city's central station run at night. Every night train from the central station has sleeper coaches.

Conclusions:
I. Every train that leaves the central station has sleeper coaches.
II. Some trains that leave the central station have sleeper coaches.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: The night trains are some of the station's trains, and each of them has sleeper coaches, so some trains from the station have sleeper coaches (II). Nothing is said about the trains that do not run at night, so I does not follow.
steps: Some trains are night trains; all night trains have sleepers ⇒ II
Day trains not covered ⇒ I does not follow
solution.why_others_wrong: Only I and Both extend a fact about night trains to every train; Neither misses the 'some' conclusion.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only conclusion II follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: The seats in an auditorium are numbered from 1 to 300. Rahul's seat number is a multiple of 7 and is greater than 290.

Conclusions:
I. Rahul's seat number is 294.
II. Rahul's seat number is an even number.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: The multiples of 7 between 291 and 300 are only 294 (287 is too small and 301 is beyond 300). So Rahul's seat is 294 (I), which is even (II).
steps: Multiples of 7 in 291–300: only 294 ⇒ I
294 is even ⇒ II
solution.why_others_wrong: Each 'Only' option drops a conclusion that follows from the single possible seat number.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Read the statement and the two conclusions. Assume everything in the statement to be true, and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow from it.

Statement: Ramesh's car is older than Suresh's car, and Suresh's car is older than Dinesh's car.

Conclusions:
I. Dinesh's car is the costliest of the three.
II. Ramesh bought his car before Suresh bought his.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution.concept: A conclusion must follow from the statement alone
solution.explanation: The statement compares only the ages of the cars. Price is not mentioned (I does not follow), and an older car can be bought later, for example second-hand, so the order of purchase is not given (II does not follow).
steps: Age of a car says nothing about its price ⇒ I does not follow
Age of a car ≠ date of purchase ⇒ II does not follow
solution.why_others_wrong: Each other option treats the cars' ages as if they gave their prices or purchase dates.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: Over the past month, several children in a residential colony have been bitten by stray dogs in the colony's park.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Ask the municipal body to catch the stray dogs, vaccinate them and move them to an animal shelter
Ask the children to carry sticks to the park
Cut down all the trees in the park

solution.concept: A course of action should remove the stated problem safely
solution.explanation: The problem is stray dogs biting children. Getting the authorities to catch, vaccinate and shelter the dogs removes the danger and protects both children and animals.
steps: Problem: stray dogs biting children
Remedy: authorities catch, vaccinate and shelter the dogs
solution.why_others_wrong: Closing the park punishes residents; sticks may provoke more attacks; cutting trees has nothing to do with dogs.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Ask the municipal body to catch the stray dogs, vaccinate them and move them to an animal shelter

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: A school bus picks up students at five stops in the order A, B, C, D and E, and then goes to the school. It reaches stop C at 7:40 am. It takes exactly 6 minutes to go from any stop to the next, and also 6 minutes from stop E to the school. It does not wait at any stop.

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: The bus leaves stop A at 7:30 am
The bus reaches the school at 7:58 am
The bus carries the same number of students every day
Classes at the school begin at 8:00 am

solution.concept: An inference must follow from the given facts alone
solution.explanation: From C (7:40 am) the bus needs three more 6-minute legs: C to D, D to E and E to the school, so it arrives at 7:58 am.
solution.why_others_wrong: The bus leaves A at 7:28 am, not 7:30; the number of students and the school's starting time are not given.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The bus reaches the school at 7:58 am

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Claim: Installing a drinking-water cooler in the school playground will make students drink more water during the games period.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the claim?

options.text: The water cooler will cost the school ₹20,000
At present, students who want water during the games period must walk back to the main building, and most of them do not do so
Students play football and cricket during the games period
Some students bring water bottles from home

solution.concept: Strengthen: show that the distance to water is what stops students from drinking
solution.explanation: If students drink little now because the water is far away, a cooler in the playground removes that obstacle, so they are likely to drink more.
steps: Claim: cooler ⇒ more drinking
Strengthener: distance is the obstacle now
solution.why_others_wrong: The cost and the games played are irrelevant; students who bring bottles already have water, which, if anything, weakens the claim.
solution.final_answer: Option B: At present, students who want water during the games period must walk back to the main building, and most of them do not do so

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: There is no pedestrian crossing on the busy road outside a city hospital, and patients' relatives often run across the road between moving vehicles.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Mark a pedestrian crossing with a signal near the hospital gate and post a traffic warden there at busy hours
Shift the hospital to another part of the city
Stop patients' relatives from visiting the hospital
Close the road to all vehicles permanently

solution.concept: Practical remedy for the stated danger
solution.explanation: The danger is pedestrians crossing a busy road with no safe crossing. A signalled crossing with a warden lets people cross safely without disrupting the hospital or the road.
steps: Problem: no safe place to cross
Remedy: signalled crossing + warden
solution.why_others_wrong: Moving the hospital, banning visitors and closing the road are extreme and impractical.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Mark a pedestrian crossing with a signal near the hospital gate and post a traffic warden there at busy hours

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: A company introduced flexible office hours in January. In January–March, employee absence was 15% lower than in October–December of the previous year. So the flexible hours reduced absence.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

options.text: Most employees said they liked the flexible office hours
In each of the past five years, absence at the company in January–March was about 15% lower than in the October–December quarter before it, because of the festival and flu season in October–December
A rival company introduced flexible office hours last year

solution.concept: Weaken: show that the fall would have happened anyway
solution.explanation: If absence always falls by about 15% from October–December to January–March, the fall this year is the usual seasonal pattern and does not show that flexible hours made a difference.
steps: Evidence: 15% fall after the change
Weakener: the same fall happens every year ⇒ no effect shown
solution.why_others_wrong: Employees liking the hours does not show lower absence; the company's size and a rival's policy are irrelevant.
solution.final_answer: Option B: In each of the past five years, absence at the company in January–March was about 15% lower than in the October–December quarter before it, because of the festival and flu season in October–December

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: Among the four branches of a bank in a town, the Station Road branch has more customers than the Market branch, and the Market branch has more customers than the Hospital Road branch. The Lake View branch has fewer customers than the Hospital Road branch.

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?

options.text: The Market branch has the most customers of the four
The Lake View branch has the most deposits of the four
The Station Road branch has more customers than the Lake View branch
The Hospital Road branch has fewer customers than the Lake View branch

solution.concept: Chain the comparisons
solution.explanation: Station Road > Market > Hospital Road > Lake View, so Station Road has more customers than Lake View.
steps: Station Road > Market > Hospital Road
Hospital Road > Lake View
⇒ Station Road > Lake View
solution.why_others_wrong: Station Road, not Market, has the most customers; deposits are not mentioned; Lake View has fewer customers than Hospital Road, not more.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The Station Road branch has more customers than the Lake View branch

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: Every year, tomato prices in a district crash in the same two months because the whole harvest reaches the market at once, and many farmers sell at a loss.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Ban tomato farming in the district
Ask farmers to destroy part of their harvest every year
Bring tomatoes from other states into the district's markets
Help farmers' groups sign supply contracts, fixed before the season, with tomato-processing units that make puree and ketchup

solution.concept: Address the glut without harming farmers
solution.explanation: Prices crash because too many tomatoes reach the market at once. Contracts with processing units give farmers a fixed outlet and price for part of the crop, so less of it floods the market.
steps: Problem: glut at harvest time
Remedy: assured outlet through processing contracts
solution.why_others_wrong: A ban is extreme; destroying crops wastes produce and income; importing tomatoes worsens the glut.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Help farmers' groups sign supply contracts, fixed before the season, with tomato-processing units that make puree and ketchup

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: Residents of Ward 7 visit the city's government hospital less often than residents of any other ward. So the people of Ward 7 are the healthiest in the city.

Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument?

options.text: Ward 7 is the farthest ward from the government hospital, and most of its residents are treated at a large private clinic inside the ward
Ward 7 has more parks than any other ward
The government hospital has added 100 beds this year
Residents of Ward 7 visit the hospital mainly for check-ups

solution.concept: Weaken: give another reason for fewer hospital visits
solution.explanation: If Ward 7's residents go to a nearby private clinic instead of the distant government hospital, they may fall ill as often as anyone else; the low number of hospital visits does not show better health.
steps: Evidence: fewer visits to one hospital
Weakener: they are treated elsewhere ⇒ visits do not measure health
solution.why_others_wrong: More parks would, if anything, support the argument; hospital beds and the purpose of visits do not explain why Ward 7's visits are fewer.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Ward 7 is the farthest ward from the government hospital, and most of its residents are treated at a large private clinic inside the ward

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Argument: The city plans to replace its diesel buses with electric buses, claiming that this will reduce the amount of fine dust in the city's air.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the claim?

options.text: Electric buses cost more to buy than diesel buses
Studies of the city's air show that exhaust from diesel buses is a major source of the fine dust along the main bus routes
Electric buses are quieter than diesel buses
Many cities abroad have started using electric buses

solution.concept: Strengthen: link the thing removed to the problem
solution.explanation: Electric buses produce no exhaust. If diesel-bus exhaust is a major source of the fine dust, removing it should reduce the dust.
steps: Claim: electric buses ⇒ less fine dust
Strengthener: diesel exhaust is a major source
solution.why_others_wrong: Cost and noise do not bear on dust; what other cities do says nothing about this city's air.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Studies of the city's air show that exhaust from diesel buses is a major source of the fine dust along the main bus routes

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Passage: In a bank's recruitment drive, a candidate is shortlisted only if he or she clears both the written test and the group discussion. All 200 candidates took both. 120 cleared the written test and 90 cleared the group discussion.

Which of the following must be true?

options.text: At least 100 candidates cleared neither stage

solution.concept: 'Only if' gives a necessary condition, not a sufficient one
solution.explanation: A shortlisted candidate must have cleared both stages, and at most 90 candidates (those who cleared the group discussion) can have cleared both. So at most 90 were shortlisted. At least 120 + 90 − 200 = 10 cleared both, but clearing both does not guarantee shortlisting ('only if'), so even 'at least 10 shortlisted' is not certain.
steps: Shortlisted ⊆ cleared both ⊆ cleared the group discussion (90) ⇒ at most 90
Cleared both ≥ 10, but 'only if' ⇒ shortlisting not guaranteed
solution.why_others_wrong: Exactly 90 treats clearing both stages as enough for shortlisting; at least 120 candidates cleared some stage, so at most 80 cleared neither; the number who cleared both is at least 10, not exactly 10.
solution.final_answer: Option C: At most 90 candidates were shortlisted

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Statement: An inspection found that many fire extinguishers in the city's shopping malls had passed their expiry dates, and the staff of several malls did not know how to use them.

Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

options.text: Close all the shopping malls in the city
Remove the fire extinguishers from the malls
Ask shoppers to carry their own fire extinguishers
Order the malls to replace expired extinguishers within a fixed time and train their staff, and check compliance through surprise inspections

solution.concept: Fix both problems found and make sure the fix lasts
solution.explanation: The inspection found two problems — expired equipment and untrained staff. Replacing the equipment, training the staff and checking by surprise inspections addresses both and keeps the malls open.
steps: Problems: expired extinguishers; untrained staff
Remedy: replace, train, inspect
solution.why_others_wrong: Closing every mall is extreme; removing extinguishers increases the danger; shoppers cannot be expected to carry extinguishers.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Order the malls to replace expired extinguishers within a fixed time and train their staff, and check compliance through surprise inspections
